Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo></math> Sum of square of the values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> attains local maxima on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math>. and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo></math>Sum of the values of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> attains local minima on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math>. Then, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>q</mi></math> is ________

solution.text:

fx=∫−1xet−1112t−15t−27t−3122t−1061dt

Now, differentiating the above integral using Newton Leibnitz's theorem, we get,

Now, from the above diagram using first derivative test we get,

So, p=0+4=4, q=12+5=112
